```{=html}
<h2 id='plot.skyscapeR.starphases'>Plot seasonal stellar visibility</h2><span id='topic+plot.skyscapeR.starphases'></span>

<h3>Description</h3>

<p>Compare the seasonal visibility of one or more stars at the modelled site and epoch. Each result shows the stellar name, designation and epoch. To compare one star across epochs, compute a phase object for each year and pass the second object to plot as its second argument.
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>## S3 method for class 'skyscapeR.starphases'
plot(
  x,
  y,
  show.labels = TRUE,
  show.legend = TRUE,
  show.grid = TRUE,
  sort.by,
  pal,
  ...,
  layout = c("auto", "linear", "circular"),
  style = "publication-colour"
)
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="plot.skyscapeR.starphases_+3A_x">x</code></td>
<td>
<p>A star phase result.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="plot.skyscapeR.starphases_+3A_y">y</code></td>
<td>
<p>A second object of <em>skyscapeR.starphases</em> format or
a list of <em>skyscapeR.starphases</em> objects for plotting (see Examples).</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="plot.skyscapeR.starphases_+3A_show.labels">show.labels</code></td>
<td>
<p>Logical. Mark annual events for a single result in either layout. Defaults to TRUE.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="plot.skyscapeR.starphases_+3A_show.legend">show.legend</code></td>
<td>
<p>Show a legend for seasons present among the plotted
stars (default TRUE). For circular plots FALSE also hides titles, site/epoch text and all layer or event callouts. The seasonal scale stays visible. Linear plots keep their data and event labels.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="plot.skyscapeR.starphases_+3A_show.grid">show.grid</code></td>
<td>
<p>Draw monthly dividers through each ring or strip. Defaults to TRUE.
Set FALSE to omit the monthly divisions and retain the seasonal axis.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="plot.skyscapeR.starphases_+3A_sort.by">sort.by</code></td>
<td>
<p>Optional ordering by catalogue magnitude (<code>"mag"</code>), first R-only
sample (<code>"rise"</code>) or first S-only sample (<code>"set"</code>) on the stored
cycle. This is not sorting by the dated heliacal event. Missing classes are
placed last; omission retains input order.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="plot.skyscapeR.starphases_+3A_pal">pal</code></td>
<td>
<p>Five colours in the order RS (rise and set), R (rise only), S (set only),
V (curtailed passage) and I (arising and lying hidden). The default uses five colours from the plot style. Monochrome adds textures to distinguish the classes. Supply all five even when only some
seasons occur.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="plot.skyscapeR.starphases_+3A_...">...</code></td>
<td>
<p>Additional arguments to be passed to <em>plot</em>.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="plot.skyscapeR.starphases_+3A_layout">layout</code></td>
<td>
<p><code>"auto"</code> and <code>"circular"</code> draw a single ring or concentric rings
in input (or requested sort) order from the outside inward. Leaders connect the layer identifiers
to their rings. Select <code>"linear"</code> for strips. Supply this argument by name.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="plot.skyscapeR.starphases_+3A_style">style</code></td>
<td>
<p>Analytical display style, either <code>"publication-colour"</code> (default) or
<code>"publication-mono"</code>. Monochrome uses grayscale and preserves line styles.</p>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Details</h3>

<p>Read each colour as a daily model classification: visible rising and setting, rising
only, setting only, visible without a qualifying near-horizon passage, or invisible. The
function plots the stored phase sequence on a 365-day scale and can label seasons or
display a legend. A single result defaults to a circular view, advancing clockwise
from December solstice. Further results use concentric rings with one leader per displayed layer;
optional sorting uses the stored apparent magnitude or seasonal onset. Changing the
display does not recalculate the visibility thresholds. Use <code>plot(first, list(second, third))</code> to compare results.
</p>


<h3>Value</h3>

<p>Draws on the active graphics device and returns NULL invisibly.
</p>


<h3>Validation</h3>

<p>W01 checked season boundaries, event positions, quarterly landmarks and star, site and epoch labels in linear and circular layouts. See the <a href="#w01-plot-geometry">W01 check in the technical manual</a>.
</p>


<h3>Seasonal axis and comparison</h3>

<p>The axis is a 365-sample synthetic solar-longitude cycle anchored at December
solstice. Equinoxes and solstices mark quarter-cycle positions. The monthly
dividers mark twelve equal intervals of 30 degrees in solar longitude,
beginning at December solstice. For calendar dates use the underlying result's
<code>metadata$events$date.julian</code>, as described in <code>star.phases</code>.
</p>
<p>Objects may represent different stars, epochs, sites or model assumptions.
Shared star, epoch and site appear once. Different epochs of the same star label individual rings or rows. Mixed comparisons identify both star and year. Hold the site,
extinction and other inputs fixed for a controlled epoch comparison, or
state their differences in the figure caption. Names on the supplied list can
override the displayed star names. The legend contains only the union of
season classes present in the plotted objects.
</p>
<p>Event annotations follow the event table. The Schaefer first-morning and last-evening markers use the solar longitude of the predicted local date. Passage bands and the two other markers follow the Purrington seasonal classification. See <a href="heliacal-rising.html#v01-observations">V01 observed dates and scientific checks</a>.
A single ring labels each event by name on two lines just outside the rim.
Its short leader meets the ring at the event's model day. A single ring shows the star, epoch and site in its centre. Rings for one star at several epochs show the star, designation and shared site in the centre, with a year for each ring. The circular layout
labels the solstices and equinoxes outside its rim. Both layouts mark the event's model day,
as recorded in the event table.
The linear seasonal scale sits immediately below the lowest strip. Each quarter
label aligns with its solstice or equinox across every row. Rising-event labels
sit close above a single strip and setting-event labels close below it, leaving
room for the seasonal scale where needed. Both layouts use the same
sequence and colours; the circular layout makes the cycle boundary explicit.
Labels wrap and shrink to fit; crowded comparisons need a larger device.
</p>


<h3>See Also</h3>

<p><code>star.phases</code>
</p>


<h3>Examples</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>## Not run: 
if (requireNamespace("swephRdata", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # Plot the seasonality of Aldebaran for 4001 BCE:
  s1 &lt;- star.phases('Aldebaran',-4000, c(35,-8, 200))
  plot(s1) # circular by default
  plot(s1, layout="linear")
  # Plot seasonality of several stars
  s2 &lt;- star.phases('Alnilam',-4000, c(35,-8, 200))
  s3 &lt;- star.phases('Elnath',-4000, c(35,-8, 200))
  plot(s1, s2)
  plot(s1, list(s2,s3))
  plot(s1, show.legend=FALSE, show.grid=FALSE)
}

## End(Not run)
</code></pre>

```
